title: CST-128: globally capped shift testing with linear workspace

claims.statement: For CST-128 in proof.md, with k=n+4 tests per candidate, global acquisition cutoff 128N and n=ceil(log2 N), for every N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery has probability greater than 29/32. All constants are absolute and all four branchwise bounds hold jointly for this same algorithm/configuration under the clean-input model. Worst-case total charged sequential work T(N,s)=O(N n^2), hence the uniform envelope B_T(n)=2^n n^2. Its exact growth index is 1.

For CST-128 in proof.md, with k=n+4 tests per candidate, global acquisition cutoff 128N and n=ceil(log2 N), for every N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery has probability greater than 29/32. All constants are absolute and all four branchwise bounds hold jointly for this same algorithm/configuration under the clean-input model. Worst-case peak allocated classical storage S_C(N,s)=O(n) bits, with envelope B_C(n)=n and exact growth index 0.

For CST-128 in proof.md, with k=n+4 tests per candidate, global acquisition cutoff 128N and n=ceil(log2 N), for every N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery has probability greater than 29/32. All constants are absolute and all four branchwise bounds hold jointly for this same algorithm/configuration under the clean-input model. Worst-case peak allocated accessible quantum storage S_Q(N,s)=O(n) qubits, with envelope B_Q(n)=n and exact growth index 0.

For CST-128 in proof.md, with k=n+4 tests per candidate, global acquisition cutoff 128N and n=ceil(log2 N), for every N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, unconditional full-secret recovery has probability greater than 29/32. All constants are absolute and all four branchwise bounds hold jointly for this same algorithm/configuration under the clean-input model. Total acquired source copies Q(N,s)<=128N<=128*2^n on every branch, including all discarded copies and failed tests. The uniform envelope B_samples(n)=2^n has exact growth index 1.

For the same CST-128 algorithm and configuration in proof.md, for every N>=2 and every s in Z/NZ, the guaranteed malformed-sample fraction is epsilon(n)=0. Every acquired copy is an independent ideal coset state; at most floor(epsilon(n) Q)=0 copies may be malformed. Under this promise, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability greater than 29/32 jointly with all four stated branchwise resource bounds. No positive tolerance or maximum-tolerance claim is asserted.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
